clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s dominant problem is early CKD driven by longstanding insulin‑requiring diabetes and hypertension. This underlies most of the metabolic derangements and raises cardiovascular risk, explaining the need to prioritize CKD management. Secondary considerations include sub‑clinical coronary disease, uncontrolled hypertension (including possible masked or secondary forms), and sub‑optimal diabetes control, all of which compound renal injury. Metabolic syndrome, early HFpEF, OSA, NAFLD, and peripheral arterial disease are plausible but lack objective confirmation. Preventive gaps (vaccinations, cancer screening) and modifiable factors (medication adherence, dyslipidaemia, vitamin D status) are also highlighted. Unexplained urine findings remain unresolved and require focused repeat testing.
